Empirical Research Plan: Schooling, College Proximity, and Earnings (NLS Young Men)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Method: Two–Stage Least Squares (Instrumental Variables).

Justification  
• The policy‐relevant “treatment” (years of schooling) is chosen by individuals and therefore endogenous (ability bias, family background, reverse causality).  
• Geographic proximity to a college in adolescence is plausibly exogenous once we condition on birthplace characteristics and cohort.  
• Distance shifts the probability of attending/finishing college but should not affect later earnings through any other channel except schooling.  
Hence, distance (or the presence of a college within a given radius) is a strong, plausibly exogenous instrument that delivers a Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) for “compliers”.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Endogenous treatment (D): Years of completed schooling (continuous).  

Instrument (Z): “Near College” – indicator = 1 if a 4-year college was located within 25 miles of the individual’s home (county of residence at age 14) in the year he turned 17; 0 otherwise. Alternative, continuous instruments: log(distance), number of colleges within 25 miles.

Control / counterfactual group: Individuals without a nearby college (Z=0).  
Because the IV design is fuzzy, timing is not an issue (cross-section). There is no running variable/cut-off in the RDD sense.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Relevance: Nearness to a college raises schooling (Cov(Z,D)≠0).  
Plausibility: Historically very few students relocated solely for school; empirical F-stat > 10 expected.

A2. Independence (quasi-random assignment): Conditional on observed background (race, parental education, birth region, urbanicity) the instrument is as good as randomly assigned with respect to unobserved determinants of earnings.  
Plausibility: Parents rarely choose residence anticipating later college returns; use birthplace rather than current address to reduce migration bias.

A3. Exclusion Restriction: Conditional on controls, proximity affects earnings only through schooling (no direct labor-market effects).  
Plausibility: Youth surveyed in the 1960s were largely mobile in adulthood, and most colleges are not major employers in their counties; nonetheless must test.

A4. Monotonicity: Living closer weakly increases schooling for everyone (no “defiers”).  
Plausibility: Reasonable—nobody will complete fewer years of school solely because a college opened nearby.

A5. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA): One person’s instrument value does not affect another’s potential outcomes (no general equilibrium in college markets at national scale).  
Plausibility: With dispersed population this is credible.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Selective Migration / Sorting  
• Strategy: Use county of birth / address at age 14 (pre-decision).  
• Robustness: Restrict to individuals whose parents were also born in the same county; include parental characteristics & county-of-birth fixed effects.

T2. Instrument correlated with local labor-market conditions (college towns)  
• Strategy: Control for county-level 1960 log manufacturing wages, unemployment, population density.  
• Robustness: Placebo regressions – test whether proximity predicts earnings of men who did not obtain additional schooling.

T3. Omitted ability/family background still correlated with distance  
• Strategy: Rich vector of family controls (parental education, occupation, family income at age 14).  
• Robustness: Balance tests; show “Near College” does not predict AFQT scores or parental earnings.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline (executable)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)      # fast IV
library(modelsummary)

# 1. Data -----------------------------------------------------------------
nls <- read_csv("nls_young_men.csv")

# 2. Variable construction -------------------------------------------------
nls <- nls %>% 
  mutate(near_college  = if_else(distance4yr <= 25, 1, 0),
         yrs_schooling = educ_years,
         ln_earn       = log(earnings_real),
         cohort        = factor(birth_year),
         region_birth  = factor(region_birth))

# 3. Baseline IV -----------------------------------------------------------
iv_baseline <- feols(ln_earn ~ yrs_schooling + race + parental_ed + 
                       parental_inc + region_birth | 
                       . ~ near_college,        # first stage: yrs_schooling ~ near_college + X
                     data = nls, 
                     cluster = ~region_birth)

etable(iv_baseline, stage = 1:2, se = "cluster")

# 4. First-stage F-statistic
iv_first <- fitf(iv_baseline)   # in fixest, fitf extracts F
print(iv_first)

# 5. Robustness: alternative instrument – number of colleges within 50 mi
nls <- nls %>% mutate(colleges50 = if_else(is.na(ncol50), 0, ncol50))
iv_alt <- feols(ln_earn ~ yrs_schooling + controls | . ~ colleges50, 
                data = nls, cluster = ~region_birth)

# 6. Placebo test: outcome = parental earnings (should be zero)
placebo <- feols(parental_inc ~ yrs_schooling | . ~ near_college, 
                 data = nls, cluster = ~region_birth)

modelsummary(list(Baseline = iv_baseline, AltInst = iv_alt, Placebo = placebo),
             statistic = "std.error", gof_omit = "IC|Adj")

```

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Economic theory predicts a positive return to schooling; U.S. micro estimates for this cohort hover around 7–10 percent per additional year.  
Prior: β ≈ 0.08 (elasticity of earnings w.r.t. schooling) in the IV specification; larger than OLS because IV identifies a LATE for marginal students.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (IV)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C1 – Instrument relevance (first-stage F > 10):                         1  
C2 – Instrument exogenous to unobserved ability/family factors:         0  
C3 – Exclusion (no direct earnings effect other than via schooling):    0  
C4 – No differential selective migration around instrument:             1  
C5 – Monotonicity (no defiers):                                         1  

Aggregate score: 3 / 5 – credible but still requires careful robustness checks and transparent reporting.
